required_revisions.text: Matched-input baselines. If any baseline cannot be run on the richer inputs, say so and explain why. If these runs cannot be completed, the abstract, introduction and discussion must be rewritten so that no claim of superiority over baselines is made — the comparison should then be presented explicitly as method-plus-input versus method-on-M1.

Ethics and consent disclosure. Add an Ethics Statement to the main text giving the IRB/oversight committee name and protocol number (the authors state they will seek institutional permission; if identifiers genuinely cannot be released, state that explicitly and name the institution type and DTA status), and an explicit informed-consent statement — consent obtained, IRB-approved waiver, or biobank/secondary-use coverage. Add a funding disclosure or an explicit 'no external funding' statement. Also state whether the cohort is retrospective or trial-linked; if any samples derive from an interventional study, give the registration.

Paired statistics for all headline comparisons. minor_suggestions: State plainly, in one or two sentences in the introduction or related work, what LATTICE does that GraphST or STAGATE with concatenated multimodal input cannot — the rebuttal's answer (per-block masked reconstruction targets, cross-modal alignment between assay views of the same spot, modality-specific adapters into a shared encoder) is convincing and belongs in the paper.
Soften 'key limitation' framing of prior work in the introduction, per the authors' own offer, so positioning matches the incremental-but-real nature of the contribution.
Move the compact 'modality block' definition and a ReCAST-vs-SARSIM division-of-labour table to Section 1, immediately after the modality ladder is introduced.

Add foundational masked-autoencoder and multimodal contrastive citations (MAE, BERT, SimCLR/CLIP) alongside the NCE reference, and attribute the masked-reconstruction objective correctly — the audit notes NCE is currently the only cited source and it supports the alignment loss, not reconstruction.

Provide a data-access mechanism (contact point, DTA template, or governance route) alongside the existing statement that the cohort cannot be redistributed, so that the restriction is documented rather than absolute.

Report sequencing-level metadata where available (platform, read configuration, depth) and the reference genome build, or state clearly which of these were fixed upstream by the collaborating institution and are unknown to the authors.
Consider noting whether any batch correction across samples or modality blocks was applied; the audit found this unaddressed.

weaknesses.text: The abstract uses 'LATTICE' and 'multimodal spatial omics integration' without defining them in the abstract itself, making it less self-contained. The abstract should state upfront that LATTICE is a graph neural network method, not just name it.

The relationship between ReCAST and SARSIM is mentioned in the introduction (Section 1) but their roles are not clearly delineated until Section 4.1 and Appendices F–G. A reader cannot determine from the main text alone which preprocessing steps are performed by which tool, creating ambiguity about the method's scope.

The term 'modality blocks' is used before it is formally defined. Section 3.1 introduces X^(b) as 'modality block b' but does not explain what constitutes a 'block' (is it a set of features? a matrix?) until Section 4.1 lists the five blocks explicitly.

Section 4.1 states 'ReCAST performs preprocessing and harmonization' and 'SARSIM performs spatially anchored regulatory projection,' but the main text does not specify which steps are internal to LATTICE and which are upstream. This makes it unclear whether LATTICE's contribution includes the harmonization or only the graph SSL training.

Table 1 caption and text do not explain what 'Multiome cells' represents (is it the number of cells profiled? cells mapped to spots?). The column 'Final intersected genes' varies from 129–322 across samples, but the text does not explain why this variation occurs or whether it affects comparability.

Figure 2 shows trends across M1–M5 but the y-axis ranges differ across panels (e.g., ARI and NMI both 0–1.0, but spatial contiguity also 0–1.0 despite different semantics). The figure caption does not explain what 'cohort mean ± std' means operationally (is it mean across 11 samples? across runs within samples?).

The Multimodal Utility Score (MUS) is introduced in Section 4.1 (Eq. 11) as averaging four normalized quantities, but the normalization procedure is deferred to Appendix A.2. A reader cannot assess whether MUS is a reasonable metric without reading the appendix, and the main text does not justify why these four components were chosen or weighted equally.

Section 4.2 states 'Adding projected scMultiome RNA to Visium RNA improves ARI, NMI, spatial contiguity, silhouette, and MUS' but does not provide the actual numbers in the main text—readers must consult Table 2. The claim would be stronger if the main text stated the magnitude (e.g., 'ARI improved from 0.269 to 0.426, a gain of +0.157').

The ablation study (Table 3) removes components from the full M5 model, but the table caption does not explain what 'Spatial reg.' and 'Masking' mean operationally (are these loss terms? architectural components?). A reader unfamiliar with the method cannot interpret the rows without re-reading Section 3.3.

Section 4.3 claims 'Paired pre/post-treatment samples show patient-specific shifts' and 'global shift alignment is near zero,' but these quantities are not defined or quantified in the main text. What is 'global shift alignment'? How is it computed? The reader must infer this from Figure 3 alone, which is insufficient.

The paper uses 'Space Ranger clusters' as a reference label in Section 4.1 but does not explain whether Space Ranger is a tool, a method, or a dataset. The text should clarify that Space Ranger is 10x Genomics' standard RNA-only clustering pipeline (this is stated in a footnote but should be in the main text).

Appendix I (Theoretical Analysis) provides lemmas and a theorem but these are not referenced in the main text and their relevance to the empirical results is unclear. If the theory is meant to justify the method, the main text should cite it; if it is supplementary, the appendix should be clearer about its role.

questions: In Section 1, the paper states that LATTICE 'constructs a spatial neighborhood graph and trains a TransformerConv encoder using masked reconstruction, cross-modal alignment, and spatial smoothness objectives.' Are all three objectives always used, or are they optional? Table 3 ablates them, but the main text does not state whether the default configuration uses all three.

Section 4.1 defines the modality ladder M1–M5 and states 'Levels M2 to M3 align with the SARSIM-scope inputs, and levels M4 to M5 add ReCAST-derived in situ epigenomics.' Does this mean SARSIM produces M2–M3 and ReCAST produces M4–M5? Or do both tools contribute to all levels?

Table 1 shows 'Final intersected genes' ranging from 129–322. The text states (Appendix H) that 'the final intersected gene set is sample-specific' but does not explain why. Is this due to quality filtering? Availability of features in each modality? This affects the comparability of embeddings across samples.

Figure 2 shows that ARI and NMI decrease from M2 to M5, while spatial contiguity increases. The text interprets this as the embeddings capturing 'chromatin and regulatory structure beyond transcriptomic similarity alone.' But how do you distinguish between (a) the embeddings capturing real biological signal that RNA-only methods miss, and (b) the embeddings diverging from the RNA reference due to noise or misalignment in the chromatin modalities?
Section 4.3 states 'leave-one-patient-out prediction is mixed' but does not define what is being predicted or what 'mixed' means quantitatively. Can you provide the actual prediction accuracy or AUC?

Appendix I provides theoretical analysis (Lemmas I.1–I.4 and Theorem I.4) but these results are standard (spatial smoothness from graph Laplacian, reconstruction consistency from autoencoders, alignment from NCE). Are these meant to be novel theoretical contributions, or are they provided for completeness? The main text should clarify their role.

The paper states that LATTICE is 'modular with respect to multimodal feature construction' and 'compatible with a range of upstream integration or mapping strategies' (Section 3.4). But all experiments use ReCAST and SARSIM. Has the method been tested with alternative upstream pipelines, or is this a claim about potential rather than demonstrated compatibility?

weaknesses.text: Table 2 reports cohort-level means and standard deviations (e.g., 'ARI 0.426±0.075' for LATTICE M2) but does not state whether these are computed across the 11 samples, across multiple runs per sample, or both. The text states 'joint multisample analysis uses seed 7 and reports stability summaries over 11 analysis seeds' (Appendix H), but it is unclear whether the ±values in Table 2 reflect inter-sample biological variation, inter-seed algorithmic variation, or a combination. This is a HARD issue because the denominator for the standard error is undefined.

The multimodal utility score (MUS, Eq. 11) is a weighted average of four normalized metrics (spatial contiguity, silhouette, same-cluster spatial-neighbor fraction, and embedding k-NN/spatial k-NN Jaccard overlap). No justification is given for equal weighting (1/4 each), no sensitivity analysis shows how MUS changes if weights are perturbed, and no external validation demonstrates that this composite metric correlates with downstream biological utility. This is a SOFT issue (a better approach would include weight sensitivity or biological validation), but it undermines the claim that M5 has 'highest MUS' without knowing whether the weighting is arbitrary.

Figure 2 and Table 2 show that ARI and NMI decrease from M2 to M5 (e.g., ARI drops from 0.426 to 0.329), and the authors interpret this as evidence that 'the learned embeddings capture regulatory and chromatin structure beyond transcriptomic similarity alone.' However, no statistical test is provided to determine whether this decrease is significant or whether it could reflect noise or overfitting. A paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test across the 11 samples comparing M2 vs M5 ARI values would clarify whether the drop is real. This is a HARD issue because the interpretation hinges on a quantitative claim without a test.

Table 3 (ablation) reports metric changes when spatial regularization or masking are removed (e.g., spatial contiguity drops from 0.850 to 0.783 when spatial regularization is removed), but no p-values or confidence intervals are provided. It is unclear whether these differences are statistically significant or merely noise. A paired test across the 11 samples would be appropriate here. This is a HARD issue.

The baseline comparisons in Table 2 include methods (GraphST, STAGATE, SpaGCN, SIMO, MaxFuse) applied to the same cohort. However, the text does not state whether hyperparameters for these baselines were tuned on the same data, whether cross-validation was used to select hyperparameters, or whether the reported numbers represent the best configuration found. If hyperparameter tuning was done on the evaluation data, this introduces leakage. This is a HARD issue if leakage occurred; a SOFT issue if tuning was done on a held-out set or pre-specified.

Section 4.3 reports 'leave-one-patient-out prediction is mixed' for pre/post-treatment shifts but provides no quantitative results, no test statistics, and no definition of 'mixed.' This is a HARD issue: a claim about cross-patient generalization requires explicit numbers (e.g., mean absolute error, correlation, or classification accuracy with a test and confidence interval).

The marker gene enrichment score (Appendix A.2) is defined but never reported in the main results or tables. It is unclear whether this metric was computed, what the values are, or how they compare across modality levels. If this metric was computed and supports the biological validity of the embeddings, it should appear in the main results; if not, its definition is orphaned.

The text states 'reproducible embeddings across analysis seeds' (Abstract) but does not quantify reproducibility. Appendix H mentions 11 analysis seeds {7, 11, 19, 23, 29, 31, 37, 41, 43, 47, 53}, but no metric (e.g., Spearman correlation of embeddings, stability of cluster assignments) is reported to measure reproducibility across seeds. This is a HARD issue because the claim is unquantified.

Spatial contiguity is defined as 'whether neighboring spots receive coherent labels' but the exact formula is not given in the main text or Appendix A.2. The definition 'SpotCut_v' appears in the MUS formula but is not expanded. Without a precise definition, the metric cannot be verified or reproduced. This is a HARD issue.

The cohort size is small (11 samples, 54,912 spots total, ~4,992 per sample). No power analysis is provided to justify this sample size for detecting the reported effect sizes (e.g., ARI improvement of +0.157 from M1 to M2). For a clinical cohort, sample size justification is important. This is a SOFT issue (power analysis would strengthen the work) but becomes HARD if any claim of 'no difference' is made from a non-significant result in this small cohort.

Figure 3 shows PCA of pre/post-treatment samples with the caption 'Shift magnitude varies by patient,' but no quantitative measure of shift magnitude is provided. The figure is qualitative; a table with shift magnitudes (e.g., Euclidean distance between pre and post centroids) and a test for whether shifts differ significantly across patients would be more rigorous. This is a SOFT issue.

The text states 'Adding scMultiome RNA to Visium RNA alone substantially improved concordance' (Abstract), quantifying this as 'ARI +0.157, NMI +0.143, spatial contiguity +0.174.' However, no test is provided to determine whether these improvements are statistically significant. A paired t-test or Wilcoxon test across the 11 samples would be appropriate. This is a HARD issue because 'substantially improved' is a quantitative claim without a p-value.

questions: In Table 2, are the reported standard deviations (e.g., '0.426±0.075' for LATTICE M2 ARI) computed across the 11 samples, across the 11 analysis seeds, or both? Please clarify the denominator and whether these reflect inter-sample biological variation, inter-seed algorithmic variation, or a combination.

For the multimodal utility score (MUS, Eq. 11), why are the four components weighted equally (1/4 each)? Have you performed a sensitivity analysis to show how MUS rankings change if weights are perturbed? Does MUS correlate with downstream biological utility (e.g., marker gene enrichment, disease outcome prediction)?

In Figure 2 and Table 2, ARI and NMI decrease from M2 to M5 (e.g., ARI 0.426→0.329). You interpret this as evidence that embeddings 'capture regulatory and chromatin structure beyond transcriptomic similarity.' Have you performed a paired statistical test (e.g., paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test across the 11 samples) to determine whether this decrease is statistically significant?

In Table 3, when spatial regularization is removed, spatial contiguity drops from 0.850 to 0.783. Is this difference statistically significant? Please provide a paired test (e.g., paired t-test) across the 11 samples with a p-value and 95% confidence interval.

For the baseline methods in Table 2 (GraphST, STAGATE, SpaGCN, SIMO, MaxFuse), how were hyperparameters selected? Were they tuned on the same cohort used for evaluation, or on a held-out validation set? If tuned on the evaluation data, this introduces leakage.

In Section 4.3, you state 'leave-one-patient-out prediction is mixed.' Please provide quantitative results: what metric was used (e.g., mean absolute error, correlation, classification accuracy)? What are the numerical values and their 95% confidence intervals?

You define a marker gene enrichment score in Appendix A.2 but never report its values. Was this metric computed? If so, what are the cohort-level values for each modality level (M1–M5), and do they support the biological validity of the embeddings?

You claim 'reproducible embeddings across analysis seeds' (Abstract) but do not quantify reproducibility. How do embeddings differ across the 11 analysis seeds? Please report a reproducibility metric (e.g., Spearman correlation of embeddings, adjusted Rand index of cluster assignments) with mean and 95% CI.

Please provide the exact formula for spatial contiguity (SpotCut_v in Eq. 11). The current definition 'whether neighboring spots receive coherent labels' is qualitative and cannot be verified without the formula.

For the claim 'substantially improved concordance' with ARI +0.157 from M1 to M2 (Abstract), please provide a paired statistical test (e.g., paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test) across the 11 samples with a p-value and 95% confidence interval. Is this improvement statistically significant at α=0.05?

In Figure 3, you show that pre/post-treatment samples separate by patient but note 'shift magnitude varies by patient.' Please quantify shift magnitude (e.g., Euclidean distance between pre and post centroids) for each patient and test whether shifts differ significantly across patients (e.g., one-way ANOVA or Kruskal–Wallis test).

What is the sample size justification for the 11-sample cohort? Have you performed a post-hoc power analysis to determine the power to detect the reported effect sizes (e.g., ARI improvement of +0.157)?

weaknesses.text: HARD: IRB committee name and protocol number are withheld for double-blind review and deferred to camera-ready version (Appendix G.3: 'For double-blind review, identifying protocol numbers and committee names are withheld'). IRB approval identifiers are a required disclosure before publication, not a camera-ready addition; this must be provided now or the manuscript cannot proceed to acceptance.

HARD: No explicit informed-consent statement is present. The manuscript states that 'Ethics and IRB oversight for human biospecimens are handled by the collaborating clinical institution' but does not confirm whether informed consent was obtained, waived, or covered under a broad biobank protocol. This must be explicitly stated.

SOFT: Funding sources are not disclosed anywhere in the manuscript. While the work may be unfunded or internally supported, an explicit statement ('no external funding' or listing of grants) should appear in a standard location (e.g., acknowledgements or a funding statement).

questions: What is the name of the IRB committee and the protocol number that approved this research? These identifiers must be disclosed in the manuscript before publication, not deferred to camera-ready.
Was informed consent obtained from all participants whose biospecimens were used? If consent was waived, what was the justification and which IRB approved the waiver?
Are there any funding sources, grants, or institutional support that should be disclosed? If the work is unfunded, please state this explicitly.

The manuscript states data are 'under a collaborator institution's proprietary agreement' — does this agreement permit the secondary use of these data for this specific research purpose, and is that use documented in the IRB approval?

weaknesses.text: SARSIM [4] is cited as a preprint with a future date (2026) and no verifiable arXiv or bioRxiv identifier, yet it is load-bearing for generating projected scMultiome RNA and ATAC blocks (M2–M3) that are critical to the pipeline, raising severe reproducibility concerns.

ReCAST is described as an internal engineering pipeline with no external reference or published paper, yet it generates spatial ATAC and spatial CUT&Tag blocks (M4–M5) that are essential inputs to LATTICE, making reproduction impossible without detailed methodology.

Masked reconstruction objective in Section 3.3 lacks citation to foundational masked autoencoder work (e.g., He et al. MAE or BERT-style masking), despite being a core component of the self-supervised learning framework.

Cross-modal alignment objective cites only NCE [12] from 2010, which is a generic contrastive principle rather than a specific multimodal alignment method; modern contrastive learning work (CLIP, SimCLR, MoCo) is not cited.
Multiple references contain future access dates (2026-05-06) for references [14], [15], and [17], which is impossible and indicates placeholder or erroneous entries.
Reference [4] (SARSIM) lacks a DOI or arXiv ID and uses a future year (2026), making it unverifiable as a real preprint.

Recent multimodal spatial omics papers from 2025–2026 (arXiv:2601.12381, arXiv:2508.00969, arXiv:2511.11730) do not appear to be cited, suggesting incomplete literature coverage of directly competing work.

Table 2 baseline comparisons do not specify which modality levels (M1–M5) were used for each baseline or whether baseline-specific hyperparameter tuning was performed, making fairness of comparison unclear.
Theoretical analysis in Appendix I presents informal lemmas and theorems without formal statements or citations to standard results in spectral graph theory, conflating novel and established results.

questions: Can you provide the actual arXiv or bioRxiv identifier for SARSIM [4]? If it is unpublished work by your group, will you commit to releasing it alongside LATTICE or provide sufficient methodological detail in the appendix for readers to reproduce the projected scMultiome block generation?

Will the ReCAST pipeline be released as open-source code? If not, can you provide a detailed methods section in the appendix describing the harmonization and quality-control steps used to generate the spatial ATAC and spatial CUT&Tag blocks?
For Table 2, can you provide a supplementary table showing which modality levels (M1–M5) were used for each baseline method and whether any baseline-specific hyperparameter tuning was performed?
Which prior work on masked autoencoders or masked language models inspired your masked reconstruction objective in Section 3.3? Please cite the specific foundational paper(s).
Beyond NCE [12], are there specific prior works on cross-modal contrastive learning or multimodal alignment (e.g., CLIP, SimCLR, MoCo) that informed your cross-modal alignment objective?

Have you reviewed the recent papers on multimodal spatial omics published in 2025–2026 (e.g., arXiv:2601.12381, arXiv:2508.00969, arXiv:2511.11730)? If so, how does LATTICE compare to or differ from these approaches?
Can you correct the future access dates in references [14], [15], and [17], and provide the correct preprint identifier and publication year for reference [4]?

For the theoretical analysis in Appendix I, can you either cite the standard results in spectral graph theory (e.g., Chung's book or recent GNN surveys) or move the informal sketches to a discussion section rather than presenting them as formal lemmas?

weaknesses.text: HARD: Baseline comparison is not conducted under matched conditions. Table 2 compares LATTICE M1 against GraphST, STAGATE, SpaGCN, SIMO, and MaxFuse, all using M1 (Visium RNA only), but then reports LATTICE M2–M5 with progressively richer inputs. This conflates two variables: (i) the LATTICE method itself, and (ii) the addition of scMultiome RNA, ATAC, spatial ATAC, and CUT&Tag. To isolate the method's contribution, baselines should be re-run on M2–M5 inputs using the same feature matrix and graph construction. Without this, the claim that 'LATTICE demonstrated stable optimization behavior' and 'substantially improved concordance' (Abstract) cannot be attributed to the method rather than to the additional modalities. The authors acknowledge that M1 to M2 shows 'the largest change' (Section 4.2), but do not test whether other methods would also improve with M2 inputs.

HARD: No external validation cohort. The entire evaluation rests on a single private 11-sample melanoma cohort. The authors state 'the raw data cannot be publicly released because of institutional data-use and privacy restrictions' (Section 4.1) and 'there is no public five-modality substitute at this lattice resolution' (Appendix G.1). This makes it impossible for readers to independently verify results or assess whether findings generalize beyond melanoma or this specific data-generation pipeline (ReCAST + SARSIM). For a method paper claiming practical utility, at least one external cohort or a synthetic benchmark with known ground truth would strengthen the claim.

HARD: The custom metric MUS is not validated against independent ground truth or external benchmarks. MUS (Eq. 11) averages four normalized quantities (spatial contiguity, silhouette, same-cluster spatial-neighbor fraction, embedding k-NN overlap). While the components are reasonable, the metric is introduced without justification for why these four terms should be equally weighted, why this particular combination captures 'multimodal utility,' or how it relates to downstream biological discovery. The fact that MUS increases with M4–M5 while ARI/NMI decrease suggests MUS may be rewarding embeddings that diverge from transcriptomic organization without evidence that the divergence is biologically meaningful. No comparison to other multimodal integration quality metrics (e.g., from the single-cell integration literature) is provided.

HARD: The claim that chromatin and histone features improve spatial organization is confounded with the possibility that they introduce noise or capture non-biological variation. Section 4.2 states: 'ARI and NMI decrease relative to M2 because the embedding no longer follows the RNA reference alone, while spatial contiguity and MUS increase.' This is presented as evidence that M4–M5 capture 'chromatin and regulatory structure beyond transcriptomic similarity alone.' However, an equally plausible explanation is that spatial ATAC and CUT&Tag signals are noisier, lower-resolution, or less biologically informative than RNA, and the method is fitting noise. The design does not include a positive control (e.g., simulated data where the ground-truth chromatin signal is known to be informative) or a biological validation (e.g., enrichment of known regulatory elements in the learned embeddings) to rule out this alternative.

SOFT: The cross-modal alignment loss (Eq. 8) is applied only to 'selected modality pairs' (Appendix H: 'modality indices zero and one correspond to Visium RNA and spatial ATAC'). The manuscript does not justify why only these two modalities are aligned, or whether aligning other pairs (e.g., scMultiome RNA with spatial ATAC, or CUT&Tag with RNA) would improve results. This is a design choice that is not ablated.

SOFT: Reproducibility across analysis seeds is reported as 'reproducible embeddings across analysis seeds' (Abstract) but the quantitative evidence is limited. Section 4.3 mentions 'leave-one-patient-out prediction is mixed' and Appendix H states that 'joint multisample analysis uses seed 7 and reports stability summaries over 11 analysis seeds {7, 11, 19, 23, 29, 31, 37, 41, 43, 47, 53},' but no table or figure shows the variance in embeddings or downstream metrics across these seeds. The standard deviations in Table 2 may reflect seed variation, but this is not explicitly stated.

SOFT: The spatial graph construction uses k=6 nearest neighbors (Appendix H) without justification or sensitivity analysis. The choice of k affects the graph structure and thus the spatial regularization loss. A brief ablation or justification (e.g., 'k=6 was chosen to match typical Visium spot density') would strengthen the design.

questions: Why were baselines not re-run on M2–M5 inputs to isolate the contribution of the LATTICE method from the contribution of additional modalities? Can the authors provide a comparison where all methods (GraphST, STAGATE, SpaGCN, SIMO, MaxFuse) are applied to the same M2–M5 feature matrix and graph as LATTICE?

Can the authors validate MUS against an independent ground truth or external benchmark? For example, do embeddings with higher MUS scores better predict downstream biological outcomes (e.g., treatment response, cell type, disease subtype) in a held-out validation set?

The decrease in ARI/NMI with M4–M5 is attributed to the embeddings capturing 'chromatin and regulatory structure beyond transcriptomic similarity.' What evidence supports this interpretation over the alternative that spatial ATAC and CUT&Tag signals are noisier or less informative? Can the authors provide a positive control (e.g., simulated data or enrichment analysis) to validate that the learned embeddings capture known regulatory relationships?
Why is cross-modal alignment applied only to Visium RNA and spatial ATAC (Appendix H)? Have the authors tested aligning other modality pairs, and if so, what were the results?

Can the authors provide quantitative evidence for 'reproducible embeddings across analysis seeds' (Abstract)? Table 2 reports standard deviations, but are these across seeds, samples, or both? A figure showing embedding stability across the 11 analysis seeds would clarify this claim.

Is there a public or synthetic benchmark dataset with known ground truth that could be used to validate LATTICE on external data? If not, can the authors discuss plans to release a subset of the melanoma cohort or create a synthetic multimodal spatial dataset for community benchmarking?

How sensitive are the results to the choice of k in the k-NN graph construction? Was k=6 chosen based on prior work, Visium spot density, or empirical tuning? An ablation across k ∈ {3, 6, 10, 15} would strengthen the robustness claims.

The manuscript states that SARSIM and ReCAST are 'internal engineering pipelines' (Section 1). How much of the improvement from M1 to M2–M5 is attributable to SARSIM/ReCAST preprocessing versus the LATTICE method itself? Can the authors quantify the contribution of each stage?

weaknesses.text: Core novelty is incremental over GraphST/STAGATE: applying masked reconstruction, contrastive alignment, and spatial smoothness to concatenated multimodal features is a straightforward extension of existing spatial graph SSL methods, not a fundamental methodological advance. The manuscript does not clearly articulate what LATTICE does that GraphST cannot do with multimodal input.

No external validation or public benchmarks: evaluation is limited to a single private 11-sample melanoma cohort (54,912 spots). No cross-dataset generalization, no public multimodal spatial omics benchmarks, no comparison to other multimodal methods on identical inputs.

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Table 2 compares LATTICE M1–M5 to GraphST, STAGATE, SpaGCN, SIMO, and MaxFuse, but all baselines use M1 (Visium RNA only) or M1 + histology. No baseline is evaluated on the full M5 multimodal input, making it impossible to assess whether LATTICE's gains are due to the method or simply to having more input modalities.

Upstream pipeline not published: SARSIM (reference [4], 'under review') and ReCAST (internal, Appendix F) are not available. LATTICE's contribution is isolated from these; independent reproduction requires reimplementing or obtaining these pipelines.

Cross-modal alignment loss uses only two modalities: Equation 8 and Section H state that alignment is computed only between 'modality indices zero and one' (Visium RNA and spatial ATAC). Why not align all modality pairs? This design choice is not justified.

Limited biological validation: Figures 4–6 show spatial domains and TF programs for one patient but do not validate whether learned embeddings capture regulatory structure beyond RNA. The divergence between ARI/NMI (which decrease with chromatin) and spatial contiguity/MUS (which increase) is noted but not explained—is the embedding learning true regulatory structure or just spatial smoothness?

MUS metric introduced without prior validation: Equation 11 combines four normalized quantities (spatial contiguity, silhouette, same-cluster neighbor fraction, embedding–spatial kNN overlap). This composite metric is reasonable but not standard; no ablation shows which components drive improvements.

Positioning overstates novelty: Abstract and introduction claim LATTICE addresses a 'key limitation' of lack of frameworks for multimodal spatial integration, but GraphST and STAGATE already integrate multiple signals (expression + spatial proximity). LATTICE's delta is the specific combination of objectives and multimodal concatenation, which is incremental.

questions: How does LATTICE perform when GraphST, STAGATE, or SpaGCN are given the same M5 multimodal input? Table 2 compares baselines on M1 only; a fair comparison requires identical inputs.
Why does the cross-modal alignment loss (Eq. 8) use only Visium RNA and spatial ATAC (modality indices 0 and 1)? Why not align all five modality pairs? Is this a design choice or a limitation?
Can you provide ablations showing the isolated contribution of each objective (reconstruction alone, alignment alone, spatial regularization alone) on the full M5 input?

What is the biological interpretation of the divergence between ARI/NMI (which decrease from M2 to M5) and spatial contiguity/MUS (which increase)? Does the embedding capture true regulatory structure, or is it learning spatial smoothness that happens to disagree with RNA-derived clusters?
How sensitive is LATTICE to the hyperparameter choices (λ₁, λ₂, λ₃, masking ratio ρ, temperature τ)? Appendix D states no sensitivity curves are included; can these be provided?
Can LATTICE be evaluated on public multimodal spatial omics datasets (e.g., 10x Genomics Visium + ATAC, or other published cohorts) to assess generalization beyond the private melanoma cohort?
SARSIM (reference [4]) is cited as 'under review' and ReCAST is internal. When will these be available? Can LATTICE be evaluated independently of these pipelines, or are they essential dependencies?

weaknesses.text: Primary dataset is private and explicitly non-redistributable: 'The cohort tensors are de-identified clinical biospecimen-derived profiles under a collaborator institution's proprietary agreement, cannot be redistributed publicly, and have no public five-modality substitute at this lattice resolution' (Appendix G.1). This is a HARD blocker for end-to-end reproduction of main results (Table 2, Figures 2–6).

ReCAST pipeline is described as 'an internal engineering pipeline' (Appendix F) with only high-level scope statements ('standardizes modality-level inputs', 'runs cross-modality gene and feature harmonization'). No pseudocode, source code link, or detailed algorithm is provided. The five-way gene intersection, harmonization procedure, and quality-control thresholds are not specified, making it impossible to reconstruct the input tensors X independently.

SARSIM is cited as a concurrent preprint (ref. [4], 'bioRxiv, 2026') with no DOI or stable link. Its role in producing 'spatially anchored regulatory projections and overlap-gene artifacts' (Appendix F) is stated but not detailed. The 'overlap_genes.txt' constraint used for harmonization is mentioned but not deposited or defined.

Code availability is promised but not yet deposited: 'We include anonymized code, Slurm driver scripts, pinned dependency manifests, and run snapshots as supplementary material' (Appendix G.1), but no repository URL, commit hash, or DOI is provided in the manuscript. Supplementary materials are not accessible to reviewers at submission time.

Processed feature matrices (X, spatial coordinates S) are not deposited. The manuscript states 'The raw data cannot be publicly released because of institutional data-use and privacy restrictions' (Section 4.1), but does not clarify whether de-identified processed tensors (after harmonization and gene intersection) could be released or whether they remain proprietary.

Upstream pipeline order and dependencies are unclear. The text states 'ReCAST performs preprocessing and harmonization, SARSIM performs spatially anchored regulatory projection, and LATTICE performs graph SSL representation learning' (Section 1), but the exact sequence of operations, which outputs feed which inputs, and how the five modality blocks are assembled from ReCAST and SARSIM outputs is not fully specified. Section 4.1 says 'For every spot, LATTICE assembles five aligned blocks' but does not detail the assembly procedure.

Modality-specific preprocessing is mentioned but incompletely specified: 'each modality block is standardized with log1p_then_zscore before concatenation' (Appendix H), but the order of operations (log1p then z-score, or z-score then log1p?), handling of zeros, and per-modality vs. global normalization are not clarified. The phrase 'log1p_then_zscore' is a configuration flag name, not a procedure definition.

Graph construction uses 'union symmetrization' (Appendix H) but this term is not defined. Does it mean (i, j) ∈ E if i ∈ kNN(j) OR j ∈ kNN(i)? This is a critical procedural detail affecting reproducibility.

Leiden clustering uses 'target cluster count K imported from SARSIM clustering metadata and achieved via a resolution sweep' (Appendix H), but the resolution sweep range, stopping criterion, and how K is determined from SARSIM metadata are not specified. This affects downstream evaluation metrics (ARI, NMI).

Masking procedure during training is incompletely specified: 'we apply random modality-block masking at the feature level' with ρ=0.15 (Appendix H), but it is unclear whether masking is applied uniformly across all features or per-modality. Does ρ=0.15 mean 15% of entries in Ω are set to 1, or 15% of each modality block? The reconstruction loss uses Huber loss with δ=1.0, but whether this applies to all modalities or only certain ones is not stated.

Cross-modal alignment pairs are underspecified: 'modality indices zero and one correspond to Visium RNA and spatial ATAC latent branches after graph refinement' (Appendix H). Are only these two modalities aligned, or are all pairs aligned? The notation in Eq. 8 suggests pairwise alignment, but the implementation detail limits it to one pair. This is a material difference affecting the loss computation.

Validation/test split is mentioned ('validation fraction is set to 0.1, with train/validation masks generated at the node level') but no test set is described. Are embeddings in Table 2 computed on the full dataset (train + validation), or is there a held-out test set? This affects the validity of reported metrics.

Downstream clustering and evaluation procedure is not fully specified: 'Predicted spot clusters are compared with Space Ranger clustering labels using ARI and NMI when overlap is available' (Appendix H). What does 'when overlap is available' mean? Are some samples excluded from ARI/NMI computation? How is this handled in Table 2 (cohort-level means)?

Ablation study (Table 3) uses 'full M5 inputs' but does not specify whether the model is retrained for each ablation or whether a single trained model is evaluated under different conditions. The row 'Spatial reg. – ✓ ✓ ✓' suggests spatial regularization is removed during training, but rows with 'Spatial ATAC at eval.' suggest modalities are withheld at test time. The distinction between training-time and test-time ablations is not clearly separated in the table caption or text.

questions: Can the authors deposit the processed, de-identified multimodal feature matrices (X, spatial coordinates S, sample metadata) at a controlled-access repository (e.g., dbGaP, EGA) with a clear access procedure, or confirm that institutional agreements prohibit this?

What is the exact procedure for ReCAST harmonization? Specifically: (i) how are gene names aligned across modalities? (ii) what are the quality-control thresholds for sample retention (3 samples were excluded; on what criteria)? (iii) how is the five-way gene intersection computed, and what is the distribution of intersection sizes across samples?
Can the authors provide a stable, versioned link (GitHub commit/tag or Zenodo DOI) to the LATTICE code and supplementary materials, including Slurm scripts and dependency files?
How is the 'log1p_then_zscore' normalization implemented? Specifically, is it log1p(X) then z-score per feature, or z-score then log1p? Are zeros handled specially?
What does 'union symmetrization' mean for the kNN graph? Is an edge (i, j) added if i ∈ kNN(j) OR j ∈ kNN(i)?

In the cross-modal alignment loss (Eq. 8), are all modality pairs aligned, or only Visium RNA and spatial ATAC? If only one pair, why were these two chosen, and how sensitive are results to this choice?

In Table 3, are the ablation rows (e.g., 'Spatial reg. –') trained from scratch with that component removed, or is a single M5 model evaluated under different conditions? Please clarify the distinction between training-time and test-time ablations.
How is the Leiden resolution sweep performed to achieve target cluster count K? What is the resolution range, and how is the final resolution selected?
Are the ARI and NMI values in Table 2 computed on all 54,912 spots, or are some samples excluded due to missing Space Ranger labels? How are cohort-level means computed if sample sizes differ?

The manuscript states 'LATTICE M1 underperforms RNA-specialized baselines because the architecture and objectives are designed for multimodal representation learning rather than optimization for transcriptomic clustering alone' (Section 4.2). Was LATTICE M1 trained with the same hyperparameters (λ₁, λ₂, λ₃) as M2–M5, or were hyperparameters tuned separately for M1?
Can the authors clarify whether embeddings Z in Table 2 are computed on the full dataset (train + validation) or on a held-out test set? If train + validation, does this inflate reported metrics?

weaknesses.text: HARD: Abstract claims 'complete multimodal integration across all samples' without defining what 'complete' means or providing quantitative evidence. No metric explicitly measures integration completeness. This is vague and unsupported as stated.

HARD: Abstract states 'LATTICE demonstrated stable optimization behavior' without defining stability or citing evidence. Section 4.2 shows early stopping spans 36–63 epochs (Appendix G.2), but no formal stability metric (e.g., variance across seeds, convergence diagnostics) is reported. The claim is unsubstantiated.

HARD: The core narrative claim—that adding chromatin and histone modalities 'improves spatial organization'—is contradicted by the authors' own data. Table 2 shows M4 and M5 have lower ARI (0.343, 0.329) and NMI (0.462, 0.450) than M2 (ARI 0.426, NMI 0.507). The authors then introduce MUS to show M4–M5 are 'better' on spatial contiguity and MUS, but this is post-hoc metric selection to rescue a declining result, not evidence that the modalities improve the embedding. The explanation that embeddings 'capture chromatin and regulatory structure beyond transcriptomic similarity alone' (Abstract) is speculation, not mechanistic evidence. This is a HARD overclaim.

HARD: Generalization scope is not acknowledged. The entire evaluation is on a single private 11-sample melanoma cohort. The abstract and conclusion claim LATTICE is 'practical and empirically grounded' and 'positions LATTICE as a general paradigm for multimodal spatial omics integration' (Conclusion), but no external validation, no other tissue types, no other cancer types, and no public datasets are used. This violates the cross-cutting rule that broad claims ('in general', 'practical framework') must acknowledge their narrow evidence base. The authors do acknowledge 'the need for stronger supervision and broader external benchmarking' (Abstract), which is good, but the framing of LATTICE as a 'practical' and 'general' framework is premature.

SOFT: The multimodal utility score (MUS, Eq. 11) is introduced only after standard metrics (ARI, NMI) show declining performance with additional modalities. While MUS is mathematically defined and transparent, its introduction appears motivated by the need to show M4–M5 are beneficial. The choice to average four normalized quantities without biological justification or prior validation is defensible but ad hoc. Why these four components? Why equal weighting? Why not use a single established metric?

SOFT: Ablation study is incomplete. Table 3 removes spatial regularization, masking, and tests modality dropout at inference, but does not ablate the cross-modal alignment loss (Lalign). The authors state 'we do not report an additional appendix grid beyond these cohort summaries' (Appendix B.1), but this is a load-bearing component of the objective and its contribution is not isolated.

SOFT: The claim that 'adding scMultiome RNA to Visium RNA alone substantially improved concordance' (Abstract) is supported by Table 2 (ARI +0.157, NMI +0.143), but the magnitude of improvement is not contextualized. Is ARI 0.426 considered 'good' clustering? How does this compare to typical spatial transcriptomics benchmarks? The term 'substantially' is interpretive without context.

SOFT: Theoretical analysis (Appendix I) makes only standard claims (spatial smoothness via graph Laplacian, reconstruction via autoencoders, alignment via NCE). Lemmas I.1–I.3 are textbook results with 'proof sketches' that do not add novel insight. Theorem I.4 is a trivial consequence of the additive objective structure. This appendix does not strengthen the contribution.

SOFT: Patient-level analysis (Section 4.3) reports that 'leave-one-patient-out prediction is mixed' and treatment signatures are patient-specific, but no quantitative results are shown. What does 'mixed' mean? What were the LOPO accuracies? This finding is important (it limits clinical utility) but is under-reported.

SOFT: The role of ReCAST and SARSIM in producing the input tensors is acknowledged, but the contribution of LATTICE itself is unclear. How much of the improvement from M1 to M2 comes from SARSIM's regulatory projection versus LATTICE's graph SSL? This is not disentangled. The authors state 'LATTICE is modular with respect to multimodal feature construction' (Section 3.4), but the dependence on upstream pipelines is not quantified.

questions: What is the operational definition of 'complete multimodal integration' in the abstract? Which metric or threshold establishes that all 11 samples achieved it?

How is 'stable optimization behavior' measured? Are there convergence diagnostics, variance across random seeds, or other quantitative stability metrics beyond the reported early-stopping epoch range?

The abstract and conclusion frame LATTICE as a 'general paradigm' for multimodal spatial omics, but evaluation is limited to melanoma. Do the authors plan external validation on other tissues, cancer types, or public datasets? If not, should the framing be narrowed to 'melanoma' or 'this cohort'?

Why was MUS introduced? Was it pre-specified in a protocol, or was it designed post-hoc after observing that ARI/NMI declined with M4–M5? If post-hoc, this is metric selection and should be disclosed.
In Table 3, why is the cross-modal alignment loss (Lalign) not ablated? This is a core component of the objective, and its isolated contribution is not shown.
What are the quantitative results for leave-one-patient-out prediction (Section 4.3)? The text states results are 'mixed,' but no accuracies or confusion matrices are provided.
How much of the M1→M2 improvement (ARI +0.157) is attributable to SARSIM's regulatory projection versus LATTICE's graph SSL? Can you disentangle these contributions?
The spatial contiguity metric is not formally defined in the main text. Is it the fraction of same-cluster neighbors in the spatial kNN graph? Please clarify in the main text, not just Appendix A.2.
Figure 3 shows pre/post-treatment separation by patient, but no statistical test is reported. Are the shifts significant? How were the PCA axes chosen?
Figures 4–6 show results for Patient 1 only. Are these representative? How do Figures 4–6 compare to the other two paired patients?
